- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) and forecast is above recent mean, lower forecast by 10–15% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence with recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3) and forecast is erratic, smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values to reduce noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 10% of forecast, adjust downward by 10–15% to reflect underestimation bias.  
- If sentiment is neutral (±0.2) and forecast is >15% above history, reduce by 5–8% to avoid false momentum.  
- If forecast is below true outcome by >5% for 3+ days, increase forecast by 2–5% to correct for underestimation bias.
